articles.title: OpenAI's Ted Sanders shares a rule of thumb for picking the right GPT-model
articles.summary: OpenAI's Ted Sanders explains where GPT-6.1 Terra fits in the company's GPT lineup. The smaller model outperforms the larger Astra in technical communication and costs far less but trails it in most other areas. Sanders says model size, reasoning effort, and multi-agent systems are distinct dimensions that can’t be reduced to a single "IQ score." The article OpenAI's Ted Sanders shares a rule of thumb for picking the right GPT-model appeared first on The Decoder.

articles.title: Zero-Shot Multimodal Event Spotting in Soccer Broadcasts
articles.summary: Automatic soccer event spotting supports highlight generation, video indexing, and sports analytics, but existing methods depend on large annotated datasets and soccer-specific training. We present a zero-shot framework that detects, classifies, and temporally localizes events in full-length soccer broadcasts without task-specific parameter training. Each match is segmented into overlapping clips represented by a compact visual storyboard and the aligned commentary transcript, which a general-purpose multimodal model processes jointly. On three manually annotated matches containing 130 events, the best configuration achieves 72.0% F1@5s and outperforms SoccerNet-trained CALF and NetVLAD++ in a cross-dataset setting, while the storyboard representation reduces inference cost by 72% compared with individual frames. We further analyze the effects of model family, input representation, and prompt optimization, and introduce an evidence-grounded excitement-scoring stage that ranks detected

articles.title: GroundControl: Satellite-Conditioned Multi-View Diffusion for Reconstruction-Free Novel View Synthesis
articles.summary: Multi-view or video diffusion models have recently emerged as state-of-the-art approaches for novel-view synthesis from sparse image collections. While they can produce high quality images, they tend to hallucinate unrealistic spatial layouts when synthesizing views outside the input views (scene extrapolation). We propose to address this challenge for outdoor scenes by using satellite images as an additional information source to condition the multi-view generative model. We introduce a new satellite-conditioned multi-view diffusion model that combines conditioning from a satellite image and street-level input images when generating novel-views. Our cross-attention based conditioning allows us to retain pretrained multi-view diffusion priors to generate seamless, realistic, novel views from a handful of source views, while also adhering to the scene layout as seen from satellite images. Our model does not use 3D scene reconstruction, and only relies on posed street and satellite views

articles.title: How Much Does the Hint Matter? A generic feedback line matches self-written critiques in hindsight self-distillation (ACM ICAIF '26) [R]
articles.summary: We study hindsight self-distillation for multi-step financial reasoning on GPT-OSS-20B. The student finds its own first wrong step and writes a critique. A frozen copy, conditioned on the prefix plus the critique, is distilled back into the student under reverse KL. Notably, replacing the critique with a fixed generic feedback line matches the full gain of about 3 points, and critiques from a 6x larger model do not materially improve performance, suggesting that the positional information provided by hindsight distillation significantly decreases the privileged information needed for effective training. Fin-SD matches OPSD from full reference solutions with 9.5% fewer tokens. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36082 | Code: https://github.com/johnnyhyu/fin-sd We'd love to find the limits of this approach. Let us know your thoughts! submitted by /u/jhzyu [link] [comments]
